agency: Guam Department of Public Health and Social Services (DPHSS), Bureau of Economic Security (BES), Division of Public Welfare
admin_note: Guam SNAP is administered centrally and territory-wide by DPHSS's Bureau of Economic Security — Guam has no counties and no sub-territory policy variation, structurally the closest analog in this roster to a single-office state-administered program (Delaware, Nebraska, Connecticut, and others), except that Guam is a full federal SNAP jurisdiction operating under its own territory-specific COLA figures rather than a 51st state. GENUINE STRUCTURAL FINDING (Guam-specific, verified against the task's own stated premise rather than assumed): this pack independently confirmed from USDA's own FY2026 COLA memorandum that Guam runs standard federal SNAP, NOT the Nutrition Assistance Program (NAP) block grant that Puerto Rico, American Samoa, and the CNMI run — Guam appears throughout the USDA memo grouped with '48 States, D.C., Virgin Islands' for INCOME ELIGIBILITY figures (net and gross FPL-based limits are IDENTICAL to the mainland, not elevated the way Alaska's and Hawaii's are), but Guam gets its OWN elevated, territory-specific figures for MAXIMUM ALLOTMENT ($1,465/mo for a household of 4, vs. $994 mainland), STANDARD DEDUCTION ($420-$598 vs. $209-$299 mainland), and MAXIMUM EXCESS SHELTER DEDUCTION ($873 vs. $744 mainland) — reflecting a higher Thrifty Food Plan cost basis for the territory, the same COLA mechanism family Alaska and Hawaii use, but applied ONLY to the benefit-calculation side, not the eligibility-threshold side, for Guam specifically. This is a genuinely asymmetric structure this pack found no secondary source describing precisely, and treats as this pack's flagship finding — see income-and-benefit-cola supplement. SECOND FINDING: DPHSS's own live, dated regulatory guidance (a January 23, 2026 official FAQ) shows Guam implemented the OBBBA's ABAWD work-requirement changes on its OWN, LATER territory-specific timeline — enforcement began January 1, 2026 with an April 1, 2026 compliance deadline, roughly two months after the November 1, 2025 date most mainland states used — while USDA's own SNAP State Options Report (17th Edition, data reference October 2024, the most recent edition available) still shows Guam holding a 'Statewide ABAWD time limit waiver' from an earlier cycle. This pack treats DPHSS's own live January 2026 FAQ as authoritative for CURRENT ABAWD enforcement status and flags the State Options Report's October-2024-dated waiver entry as likely superseded, rather than silently picking one — see abawd-work-requirement supplement. THIRD FINDING, a genuine access-difficulty disclosure rather than a correction: Guam has NO equivalent of a searchable, citable administrative-code manual this pack could locate online (no DSSM/FSM/He-W-style numbered manual the way this roster's other blank-slate states have) — DPHSS's own website (dphss.guam.gov) is thin on operative SNAP policy text beyond a services landing page, and this pack's most substantive, reliable Guam-specific primary sources turned out to be DPHSS's own numbered press releases and FAQs (hosted on the Government of Guam's official document portal, go.opengovguam.com) rather than a codified regulatory manual. This pack treats those press releases as genuinely authoritative DPHSS-authored primary sources, not secondary paraphrase, but flags that a reader wanting Guam's underlying legal citation (a Guam Code Annotated section, an Administrative Adjudication Law rule) will not find one as easily as this roster's mainland-state packs.
system: DPHSS's Bureau of Economic Security (BES), within its Division of Public Welfare, administers SNAP directly and centrally for the entire territory — Guam has no county or village-level SNAP offices with independent policy authority, consistent with USDA's own SNAP State Options Report (17th Edition) classifying Guam's SNAP program administration as 'State-administered.' Applicants can apply online, check case status, and find program brochures through the MyBenefits Guam self-service portal (mybenefits.guam.gov); DPHSS's Bureau of Economic Security can also be reached directly at (671) 300-8853 / (671) 300-8872 or centralbes@dphss.guam.gov, or in person at DPHSS's main office at 155 Hesler Place, Hagåtña, and at satellite locations DPHSS's own MyBenefits portal describes without naming individually in this pack's sources. Guam's SNAP EBT card carries its own distinctive local brand name, the 'Guam Quest Card' — this pack found no equivalent of CalFresh- or Basic-Food-style program-name branding, but the card itself is named distinctly from the generic federal 'EBT card' term. As of DPHSS's own October 2025 shutdown-FAQ press release, roughly 41,000 Guam residents — close to one-third of the territory's total population — receive SNAP benefits, a participation rate this pack flags as strikingly high relative to the states in this roster and worth surfacing directly to a reader asking about Guam's SNAP program generally.
